title: Hotrod Fishing Next Steps
lede: After the catch card fix: a river boulder that looked like glass now reads as wet stone, and a photo taken with the phone upright frames every fish whole. A shorter card was measured and would not have helped. The next step is a catch tried on your iPhone, then your pick of what to build next.

sections.title: Two fixes done, one idea measured and dropped, the rest is yours
sections.html: Asked: "NeXT steps?". The steps that needed nothing from you are done: a river boulder that looked like glass now reads as wet stone, and a photo taken with the phone upright frames every fish whole. A shorter catch card was measured and left as it is, as it would not have helped. What is left needs you: a catch tried on your iPhone, a frame rate reading, and your pick of what to build next.

sections.title: A river boulder that looked like glass
sections.html:
Catch pictures at Hotrod Landing showed a pale cyan block in the water beside the fish. It was a boulder: of the 180 that lie in water, three had their tops less than 0.7 m under the surface, and one of them lies 27 m from where you start. Light grey stone, under clear shallow water with bright caustics playing on it, showed as flat pale facets like glass.

Wet stone is darker than dry: the film of water traps light against the surface until more of it is absorbed (Lekner and Dorf, in the sources). The game already darkened the wet band just above the waterline; stone under the surface now gets the same darkening, so a submerged boulder reads as a rock under the water rather than a pale block. Dry rock, the water, the riverbed and everything else are unchanged; no rock moved.

Settling the boulder deeper was tried first, 0.8 m and then 2 m down: it stayed a pale block, only smaller, so that change was dropped. All seven water views of the regression set (Hotrod Landing, Salmon Bend, Bear Falls, Moose Lake, Glacier Lake, Halibut Pier and Moose Lake at sunset) were drawn before and after: the one visible change was the boulder at the landing (the mist differs between runs, as it follows the weather), and no shader reported an error.

sections.title: A photo taken upright frames every fish whole
sections.html:
The album kept every picture at 16 by 9. Held upright, an iPhone 15 is 393 by 852 points, so the picture was a band 338 by 190 points across the middle of the screen, and a big fish held up for a trophy shot did not fit: measured on the build before this change, every Big Skate lost about a quarter (23.4% of the smallest, 123 cm, and 24.4% of the largest, 241 cm), and the biggest halibut 5.1% (218 cm, and Barn Door, the legendary halibut, at 232 cm).

A picture taken with the screen upright is now 4 by 3: a frame 338 by 253 points, kept at 280 by 210 pixels. That is about as many pixels as the 16 by 9 picture (320 by 180), so the album takes about the same room on the phone: in the camera check the stored album was 22 KB upright against 20 KB on its side, for the same two subjects. With the phone on its side, and on a tablet or a computer held wide, nothing changes.

The stars a picture earns are measured against a 16 by 9 frame as wide (189 points tall in the check, in a frame 335 by 252), so an upright picture is no harder to fill than before: the moose 30 m away earned 3 stars upright and on its side. The viewfinder shows the taller frame, and its ● PHOTO label now sits at the top in the middle when upright, where it no longer runs under the RUN button. In the album each picture shows whole in its tile, an upright one with dark bars at its sides; tapped, it shows big as it was taken.

The catch check now fails if any of the 71 fish is cut by the photo frame on any of its nine shapes; before, it only counted them.

sections.title: A shorter catch card would not have helped
sections.html:
Upright, the catch card takes a third of the screen (279 of 852 points, measured on this build), leaving the fish 333 points above it. The plan was to make the card shorter upright, so the biggest fish could be held nearer and look bigger. Measured first, by trying all 71 fish against the room a shorter card would leave:

Card shorter byFull screen: fish held nearerFull screen: furthest any fish is heldSafari bars showing: fish held nearerSafari bars showing: furthest any fish is held
as it is (279 points tall)01.84 times01.93 times
40 points2, by up to 1.07 times1.84 times5, by up to 1.15 times1.67 times
60 points2, by up to 1.07 times1.84 times5, by up to 1.22 times1.57 times
80 points2, by up to 1.07 times1.84 times5, by up to 1.30 times1.49 times
100 points2, by up to 1.07 times1.84 times5, by up to 1.37 times1.47 times

Full screen: an iPhone 15 held upright, 393 by 852 points. Safari bars showing: the same iPhone in Safari with its bars on screen, 393 by 659 points. Furthest: against the fish's usual distance from the eye.

In full screen, 2 of 71 fish come nearer, by 7%, however much shorter the card is. Held upright, a long fish is limited by the width of the screen, not by the card: 39 of the 71 are held further out than usual on a screen 393 points wide, and a shorter card cannot change that. Only with Safari's bars showing does it help, and then for 5 of the 71 fish. So the card keeps its text and buttons at the size they are.

sections.title: Five things only you can do
sections.html:
WhatWhy it needs youHow
Try a catch on your iPhone, on its side and uprightThe catch card, the rod hand and now the upright photo were checked in a browser drawn at an iPhone's shape, never on a phone.Land a fish at Hotrod Landing on its side, then upright (turn the phone and tap PLAY IN PORTRAIT). With the camera from the Trading Post, tap PHOTO on the catch card upright too. If a fish runs under the card or out of the picture, or the hand on the rod still looks wrong, a screenshot shows which part.
Read the frame rate on your iPhoneEvery timing so far comes from a software renderer, several times slower than a phone, which says nothing certain about yours.The game starts on the High graphics setting and, with Adjust graphics automatically on, lowers the resolution and then steps down to Medium and Low by itself when frames run slow. In Settings (on the title screen or in the pause menu) turn Show frame rate on; Graphics shows the setting the game has settled on. Both, read at Bear Falls and at Hotrod Landing, tell whether your iPhone keeps High or the next round should go to speed.
Pick what to build nextSomething new to do is a choice of what the game should become, and yours to make.The three candidates are in the next section, in the order I would take them.
Say go for the App StoreYou asked me to hold the App Store preparations until you say go.The publishing guide is ready: docs/publishing.html.
Let this environment reach the web (if you want sources read in full)curl is blocked for every host here, so I read sources through web search rather than downloading them.The cloud environment menu in the session's title bar, then Edit, then Network access: a broader level, or Custom with the hosts added under Allowed domains. Steps: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#network-access.

sections.title: Something new to do: pick one
sections.html:
OptionWhat changesSizeWhy
1Mounted fish in Ruben's cabinEach species' best catch mounted on the wall of Ruben's cabin, with its weight, its length and the day it was caught: 31 places on the wall, and the 9 legendary fish in a row of their own. A wall to fill gives every species a reason to be caught again, bigger.MediumIt rewards what the game already records (your best of each species) and changes nothing in how fishing plays.
2A fishing derby at the Trading PostA contest each game week for the heaviest fish of one species, named on the board at the Trading Post, against local rivals with prize money for the top three. A game day lasts 24 minutes, so a week is about three hours of play.MediumA goal with a deadline between catches; it uses the 31 species, the 13 lures and the places that suit each fish.
3Seasons with the salmon runsThe salmon bite follows the Kenai River's runs on the game's calendar: kings from mid-May, sockeye from July to mid-August, coho from late July into October. The calendar is already there: it starts on 20 August 2026 and moves the night sky. But on the real calendar the kings would be gone for about nine game months, over 100 hours of play, so the runs would need a faster cycle of their own.LargeThe most Alaskan of the three, and the biggest change to how fishing plays; it touches the bite tables, the map's fish lists and the journal.

Today the game has 31 species, 9 legendary fish, 13 lures, 34 challenges and an odd-jobs board with three jobs at a time.

sections.title: What would change this conclusion
sections.html:
The conclusion: the next step is yours, a catch tried on your iPhone, on its side and upright, then your pick of the three options; I would start with the mounted fish. This would change if:

  • Your iPhone shows a fish under the card or out of the picture, or the hand still wrong. That comes first, from your screenshot.
  • You play upright in Safari with its bars showing. Then a shorter card on short screens would bring 5 of the 71 fish nearer, by up to 1.22 times for a card 60 points shorter.
  • Your frame rate reading is low. Then a round for speed comes before anything new.
  • You want the game in the App Store now. Then the publishing round comes first; the guide lists every step.
  • The boulder looks too dark, or still glassy, on your phone. The darkening is one number: stone under water keeps 0.68 of its colour, as the wet band just above the waterline does at its wettest.

footer:
Built on the claude/ruben-hotrod-fishing branch: the code on GitHub, the playable build and the catch card report. The boulder fix is in src/world/scatter.js (the rock material); the photo's shape is frameSize in src/gameplay/camera.js, the album tile and the viewfinder label in src/ui/styles.css.

Sources were found through web search, as curl is blocked here. Sources. Why wet stone is darker than dry: Lekner and Dorf, Why some things are darker when wet, Applied Optics 1988, https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/scps/staff/pdf/darkerwhenwet.pdf · The iPhone 15's screen in points and its safe-area insets: Use Your Loaf, iPhone 15 Screen Sizes, https://useyourloaf.com/blog/iphone-15-screen-sizes/ · When the Kenai River's salmon run: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Kenai River run timing, https://adfg.alaska.gov/Static-sf/Region2/pdfpubs/kenrun.pdf.
